  296: #### V2. The GGE Relic Without a Condensate
  297: 
  298: The GGE relic (S38 permanent result) was derived assuming a BCS condensate that forms, transits, and is quenched. At $N_{\rm pair} = 1$, the GGE remains well-defined as a statistical state, but its physical content changes.
  299: 
  300: In quenched superfluids (Paper 27, non-equilibrium vacua), the GGE describes the stationary distribution of quasiparticle occupation numbers after a rapid quench through $T_c$. The quasiparticles are excitations of the CONDENSATE. If there is no condensate, there are no quasiparticles in the Bogoliubov sense. The post-quench state is simply a single pair in an excited Fock-space eigenstate.

But the "GGE" at $N = 1$ is just the microcanonical ensemble of a single quantum walker -- its position and momentum on the lattice. The 59.8 quasiparticle pairs (S38) are an artifact of interpreting a single-pair excited state in the language of many-body BCS theory. At $N = 1$, there is 1 pair in 1 state.
